questions.q: What problem does policy as code solve?
options: It replaces the need for a human reviewer entirely
It automatically enforces rules against every plan, catching violations a manual review might miss
It speeds up terraform apply
It stores Terraform state remotely
questions.explain: Policy as code runs automated checks against every plan, catching issues that don't scale to rely on a human reviewer noticing manually each time.

questions.q: At what point in the pipeline does a policy check typically run?
options: Before terraform init
After plan and before apply
Only after apply has already completed
Only once per year during an audit
questions.explain: Policy checks evaluate the plan's output after it's generated and before apply runs, so a violation can block the change from ever being applied.

questions.q: What language are Open Policy Agent (OPA) policies written in?
options: HCL
Rego
YAML
Python
questions.explain: OPA uses its own purpose-built policy language called Rego to express rules evaluated against structured input like a Terraform plan's JSON.

questions.q: In the lesson's example Rego policy, what does the rule deny?
options: Any resource without a name
Any S3 bucket created with a public-read ACL
Any Terraform apply run outside business hours
Any resource created in the aws provider
questions.explain: The example Rego policy checks for aws_s3_bucket_acl resources being set to a public-read ACL and denies the plan if one is found.

questions.q: What is Sentinel, and how does it relate to OPA/conftest?
options: A replacement for Terraform state
HashiCorp's own policy engine built into Terraform Cloud/Enterprise, serving the same purpose as OPA/conftest but with a different language
A required dependency for using the aws provider
A tool for formatting HCL files
questions.explain: Sentinel is HashiCorp's native policy engine for Terraform Cloud/Enterprise, conceptually equivalent to OPA/conftest but using its own policy language instead of Rego.
